# Evidence audit notes — external-py-flask-tutorial

Actor: `auditor-ext2` (Independent Evidence Auditor). Draft digest audited: `1fe477e7e82d03cd27de041d127684f04e96f0a32e663f0854e9b56b0d5c289d`.

## Method

1. Read all nine in-scope Python sources in full from the pinned clone at `/home/user/legacy-spec-agent/.external-sources/flask/examples/tutorial/`: `flaskr/__init__.py` (48 lines), `flaskr/auth.py` (116), `flaskr/blog.py` (125), `flaskr/db.py` (56), `tests/conftest.py` (62), `tests/test_auth.py` (69), `tests/test_blog.py` (83), `tests/test_db.py` (29), `tests/test_factory.py` (12).
2. Wrote a Python extraction script (regex over backtick spans matching `path:line` / `path:start-end` with a citable extension) that scanned all seven staged Markdown files line by line, pulled out every `(CLM id, citation text, full markdown line)` tuple, and resolved each citation against the actual source file content so the asserted line range and its real text sat side by side for direct comparison.
3. Judged every one of the 132 tuples by hand against the source I had already read, checking whether the cited range fully substantiates everything asserted on that line — not just the general topic, but each specific sub-fact (a named behavior, a second location, an enumerated outcome).
4. Wrote a second script that emitted `staging/audit_log.jsonl` from my per-claim decisions, defaulting to `verified` and marking 14 rows `flagged`.

## Structural checks (all clean)

- Exactly 132 lines carry a CLM tag across the 7 files; every line has exactly one CLM tag and exactly one citation (no untagged citations, no double-tagged lines, no two citations sharing one CLM).
- CLM IDs 001–132 are each used exactly once; none skipped, none duplicated.
- Every cited path resolves inside the pinned clone and every cited line/range exists within the file's real line count — no out-of-range or invented citations.
- No claim presented as verified actually rests only on a non-citable file (`schema.sql`, `data.sql`, templates, `pyproject.toml`, `README.rst`). Every place the draft touches schema-only facts (DDL constraints, default-value mechanisms, foreign-key declarations, packaging metadata, run/install commands) is explicitly routed to an `UV-00x` Unverified entry with a `searched:` disclosure rather than being asserted as a cited fact. This discipline held up under scrutiny in SPEC.md, DATA_MODEL.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, ONBOARDING.md, and RISKS.md.
- Author-only authorization claims (BR-007/CLM-019, CLM-027, CLM-083, CLM-087) correctly cite `blog.py:51-55`, which is exactly `get_post()`'s `if post is None: abort(404)` / `if check_author and post["author_id"] != g.user["id"]: abort(403)` guard, called with the default `check_author=True` from both `update()` and `delete()`. These are accurate.
- Login-required claims (CLM-010, CLM-011, CLM-012) cite ranges that include the `@login_required` decorator line, and CLM-005 (anyone can view the index) cites the index route's range, which correctly has no such decorator. Config-default claims (CLM-033/034/035/036, CLM-098/099/100) all match the literal `app.config.from_mapping(...)` defaults and update path in `__init__.py`.

## Borderline claims accepted (with reasoning)

- **CLM-022** (`BR-010`, root path bound to blog index): the single cited line (`__init__.py:46`, `app.add_url_rule("/", endpoint="index")`) does not by itself explain *why* this makes `url_for('index')` resolve to the blog listing — that requires reading the adjacent comment (lines 42–45, not cited) and understanding Werkzeug's rule-matching tie-break. I accepted this because the cited line is the literal, correct piece of code performing the binding, and the claim doesn't overstate mechanics beyond what a comment two lines above (in the same function, part of the same coherent flow) already documents.
- **CLM-059** ("all submitted form fields are read via `request.form`", cited to `auth.py:54-55` only): read narrowly, this is a general architectural pattern statement illustrated by one concrete example, not an enumerated claim about every route. The identical `request.form[...]` idiom is independently and correctly cited elsewhere for every other route (CLM-067, 071, 077, 081), so I did not treat the single illustrative citation as a gap.
- **CLM-060/CLM-061** (session/cookie and process/SQLite trust boundaries): these synthesize facts already independently cited elsewhere (SECRET_KEY's signing role in CLM-033/098; the import graph in CLM-050–053 showing only `db.py` touches `sqlite3`) rather than asserting anything new and uncited. Accepted.
- **RISKS.md "Evidence:" bullets** (CLM-121–125, 128–129, 131): these follow a distinct bare-pointer structure — `- Evidence: \`path:line\` (CLM-XXX).` — separate from the sentence-level "Impact:"/"Mitigation:" bullets that carry the interpretive claim. I read the CLM's own scope as "this line is a real, on-topic piece of evidence for the finding," not "this one line alone proves every word of the neighboring Impact sentence," and all of these bare citations are accurate, on-topic single facts (a `commit()`, a `connect()`, a `close()`, an `unlink()`, an `executescript()`). I initially considered flagging CLM-127 (`test_blog.py:30`, bare-pointer to `db.commit()` while the actual `UPDATE ... SET author_id = 2` is one line above at 29) on the same theory as CLM-030/031/032, but retracted it once I recognized the bare-pointer convention — the "Impact:" sentence itself is untagged prose, and line 30 genuinely is the commit inside the same test.

## Flagged claims (14) — verdict: failed

All 14 follow one of two patterns: (a) a compound claim naming two or more specific facts/locations where the single citation demonstrably covers only one, with the other fact's real code at a distinct, never-cited line elsewhere in the same file; or (b) a citation pointing at the wrong function/line entirely.

1. **CLM-018** (SPEC.md:36, `BR-006`) — "required on **both create and update**" cites only `blog.py:69-70` (create's check). Update's identical check is `blog.py:97-98`, never cited anywhere in the draft.
2. **CLM-023** (SPEC.md:45) — "flashes an error message and re-renders the form without redirecting" cites `auth.py:59-62`, which only sets the error string. `flash(error)` is line 79, `render_template` is line 81 — neither in range.
3. **CLM-024** (SPEC.md:46) — "flashed as an error" cites `auth.py:71-74` (the `except IntegrityError` block, sets the string). `flash(error)` is line 79, not in range.
4. **CLM-025** (SPEC.md:47) — "flashed as a distinct error message" cites `auth.py:96-99` (sets the two strings). `flash(error)` is line 107, not in range.
5. **CLM-030** (SPEC.md:54) — "guarded by a non-empty title" cites `blog.py:76-80` (insert+commit only). The title guard is `blog.py:69-70`, not in range.
6. **CLM-031** (SPEC.md:55) — "guarded by author match and a non-empty title" cites `blog.py:103-107` (update+commit only). Author match is the `get_post(id)` call at line 90; the title guard is lines 97-98. Neither in range.
7. **CLM-032** (SPEC.md:56) — "guarded by author match" cites `blog.py:122-124` (db-open/delete/commit). The author-match check is inside `get_post(id)` at line 121, one line above the cited range.
8. **CLM-043** (ARCHITECTURE.md:8) — "the app reads and writes a local SQLite database file" cites only `blog.py:25` (the `render_template` return). The SQLite read (`db.execute` select) is lines 20-24, excluded from the citation; no write is shown at all by this line.
9. **CLM-054** (ARCHITECTURE.md:41) — names flask, werkzeug, **click, sqlite3, and pytest** as unresolved external edges but cites only `auth.py:1-12`, which imports flask and werkzeug. click/sqlite3 are imported in `db.py:1-4`; pytest in the test files. Neither location is cited.
10. **CLM-056** (ARCHITECTURE.md:50) — "populating `g.user` from the session" cites `auth.py:32-33`, which is only the `@bp.before_app_request` decorator and the function signature. The body that actually reads `session.get("user_id")` and sets `g.user` is lines 36-43, not in range.
11. **CLM-058** (ARCHITECTURE.md:52) — describes a flow for "**update/delete**" but cites `blog.py:86-110`, which is `update()` only; `delete()` (113-125) is never in range. Worse, the described flow ("resolve and authorize, **then validate input**, then write and commit, then redirect") is factually wrong for `delete()`, which reads no form fields and has no validation step at all.
12. **CLM-096** (DATA_MODEL.md:25) — "never set from a request field" cites `blog.py:21-23`, `index()`'s SELECT statement, which shows `created` being read/displayed but says nothing about what `create()`'s INSERT does or doesn't set. That fact depends on the INSERT at `blog.py:76-78`, not in range.
13. **CLM-113** (TESTCASES.md:34) — "Inputs: ... form data with title and body" cites `test_blog.py:19`, the `@pytest.mark.parametrize` decorator belonging to `test_login_required`, whose body (`client.post(path)`, no `data=` kwarg) sends **no form data at all**. The actual title/body form data appears in `test_create`/`test_update` (e.g. line 49), an entirely different test not cited.
14. **CLM-114** (TESTCASES.md:35) — "Expected result: 403 ..., 404 ..., redirect to the index on success" cites `test_blog.py:34-35`, which is only the two 403 assertions from `test_author_required`. The 404 case is in `test_exists_required` (line 43) and the redirect-on-success case is in `test_update`/`test_delete` (e.g. line 78) — neither cited.

## Additional observations reported, not fixed

- No cited range was absent from the source, and no line had zero/multiple CLM tags or zero/multiple citations (see Structural checks above) — the draft is clean on citation mechanics; the 14 defects above are all citation-scope/accuracy problems, not formatting problems.
- No claim relies on a non-citable file while being presented as verified — the Unverified-routing discipline held.
- The recurring shape of the defects (a citation that proves the "primary" clause of a compound sentence but omits a named second clause/location) appears concentrated in three sections: the "Validation and error behavior" and "State transitions" blocks of SPEC.md (flash/guard clauses split from their guard conditions), and compound "X/Y" or enumerated-list claims in ARCHITECTURE.md and TESTCASES.md. This is a correctable, mechanical citation-widening fix in each case (extend the range to include the omitted clause's real lines, or add a second citation if the format allowed it), not a fabrication.
